messages:
marta: Heads up — ran a small experiment this morning: splayed deploy warmers + autoscale-hooks to warm KV prefixes. Results look promising but hit a perf regression when the runtime picked quantized kernels for certain tiling shapes. TLDR: hit rate went up but some models saw throughput drops and tail latency spikes.

sahil: nice. can you share the config? how did you splay it?

marta: basically staggered starts across pods. pseudocode: for i in range(0, N): start_time = base + i * delta (delta=12s). warmers generate synthetic requests sampled from recent prefixes and replay top-k prompts. small config snippet:
```yaml
warmers:
  type: synthetic
  sample_source: recent_prefixes
  splay_delta: 12s
  concurrency: 2
  max_requests_per_prefix: 3
```

ben: did you push this to canary? any infra errors?

deploy-bot: deploy warmers/splay-2026-canary started on k8s cluster-us-east-1 at 1893005000

marta: yes, canary ran ~30m. observed KV cache thrash on pods that selected int8 quantized kernels — keying used a prefix normalization that included padding alignment; quantized kernel tiling changed token alignment so keys diverged. profiling shows p95 latency spikes coincide with kernel-selection logs.

lee: oh — kernel selection affecting cache keys is a bad tight coupling.

anita: we should canonicalize keys earlier. proposal: derive cache key from the canonical token-id sequence before any runtime-specific alignment or padding. that keeps keying invariant to kernel tiling.

sahil: agree. quick fix: move canonicalization to pre-serve path. watch the copy overhead though.

marta: did a microbench: extra copy adds ~0.6ms median per request but eliminates the mismatch. numbers from the run: baseline hit_rate=18% (no warmers). with splay warmers w/o kernel mismatch fix hit_rate=54% on non-quantized pods but effective hit_rate dropped to ~30% when quantized mismatch happened. after canonicalize-key patch hit_rate climbed to ~68% across canary and p95 improved from 210ms -> 180ms. GPU util improved on warmed pods.

ben: that improvement looks solid. can we A/B it on production for 4h?

marta: rollout proposal: canary at 10% traffic with splayed warmers enabled on canary pods. monitor metrics: kv_hit_rate, p95, gpu_util, error_rate. auto-rollback if kv_hit_rate < 40% or p95 increases >20% vs baseline.

lee: also guard against warmers triggering autoscaler feedback loops. if warmers increase CPU enough to scale, we could create more warmers => cascading starts. add a cap per-node and warmers backoff on scale events.

anita: added warmers throttle: backoff when node_pressure=true or when a scale_event happened within last 5m. warmers will set a 'seeded' flag per-prefix once prefill completes to avoid repeated work.

sahil: what about scheduled nightly prefill for heavy hitters instead of synthetic traffic? might be cheaper for stable prefixes.

marta: we tried a scheduled job at 03:00 for the top-20 prefixes — great for morning traffic but misses long-tail ad-hoc prefixes. best approach: hybrid — scheduled for heavy hitters + splay synthetic during deploys and autoscale events for opportunistic prefill.

deploy-bot: canary monitor alert: p95 increased by 5% over baseline at 1893006200 — investigate.

ben: who's oncall? @lee?

lee: @lee here. looking at traces: small subset of models (chat-lite-3b-q8) triggered kernel fallback to reference matmul at specific batch sizes causing latency spikes. need to tune kernel-selector heuristics and add fallback time budget.

anita: opened PRs: #2345 moves key canonicalization into the request front door, #2346 adds kernel-selector logs into the trace context so we can correlate selections with perf.

marta: next steps: (1) merge canonicalize-key PR; (2) add splay config to deploy templates and limit per-node concurrency; (3) schedule 4h A/B next Tue 06:00-10:00 UTC; (4) document rollback thresholds in runbook. I'll draft the runbook and share.

sahil: :thumbsup: please add metric thresholds + grafana dashboard link.

marta: added grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/abc123/warmers-splay?orgId=1

ben: also instrument kv_key_entropy so we can detect abnormal key churn and hotspots.

marta: good call — adding `kv_key_entropy` to the dashboard and alerting if it rises >2x baseline.

deploy-bot: canary completed at 1893006599. brief summary attached to the deployment ticket.

marta: thanks all — will follow up with the runbook + A/B schedule. if anyone sees odd traces, drop them here and tag the PRs.
